title: apps/alerting app.go: nil-pointer-in-interface guard for validators/mutators
answers: Why does app.go check validator != nil before assigning it?
What happens if the nil check before assigning KindValidator is removed?
body: buildKindValidator/buildKindMutator return concrete pointer types (*simple.Validator, *simple.Mutator). app.go explicitly checks `if validator != nil` before assigning into the KindValidator/KindMutator interface fields on the managed kind. Assigning a nil *simple.Validator directly into the interface field would produce a non-nil interface wrapping a nil pointer, which would break ValidateManifest's "has a mutator/validator" check downstream. Don't remove this guard as a 'simplification'.
applies: Applies specifically to buildKindValidator/buildKindMutator in apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/app.go, where these return concrete *simple.Validator/*simple.Mutator pointers that can be nil.
